bib.title: SparseGPT: Massive Language Models Can be Accurately Pruned in One-Shot

question: Can 10-100B+ parameter GPT-family models be pruned to high sparsity in one shot, without retraining, at little accuracy loss?
hypothesis: Larger models are easier to sparsify (speculated to be due to overparametrization); layerwise sparse regression can be solved approximately fast enough for 175B models.
contributions: SparseGPT, an approximate layer-wise sparse regression solver scaling to 175B parameters on one GPU
Joint sparsification and quantization in one pass
Evidence that larger models are more compressible

method.summary: Layer-wise pruning where, for each layer, columns are processed in order with a shared sequence of inverse Hessians (OBS updates on remaining weights to the right), masks chosen adaptively per block of 128 columns by OBS error. No retraining; layers processed sequentially on one A100.

datasets.name: Lambada, ARC-e/c, PIQA, StoryCloze
datasets.source: GPTQ implementation of EleutherAI eval harness

inference.samples: one pruning run per config; 5 seeds for calibration sampling only in ablation (OPT-2.7B)

parameters.lazy_update_blocksize_B: 128 (inferred: Bs matches the default lazy batch size)
parameters.pruned_layers: all linear layers, excluding embeddings and head

limits: Authors concede zero-shot numbers are noisy and a slight perplexity improvement at 175B is dataset specific (absent on PTB, C4)
Speedups are preliminary with off-the-shelf tools; GPU numbers are per-layer matmul only, end-to-end likely lower
2:4/4:8 lose noticeable accuracy on smaller models
Why larger models are easier to prune is speculation, left to future work
Only OPT and BLOOM studied; perplexity and a few zero-shot tasks, no generation quality or reasoning evals
